adhd.label: Step 1 · Jumps to Ch. 3: Bayes' Theorem & Real-World Medical Screening (Start Here)
adhd.brief: Starts with the most counter-intuitive puzzle in statistics: why a 99% accurate clinical test still produces mostly false alarms on a rare condition, and how Bayes' rule calculates the real probability.

adhd.label: Step 2 · Jumps to Ch. 5–6: Normal Distribution & The Central Limit Theorem
adhd.brief: Shows visually why averaging noisy biological measurements always converges into a clean bell curve, allowing small clinical samples to predict population truth.

adhd.label: Step 3 · Jumps Back to Ch. 1–2: Center vs. Spread (Mean, Median & Variance)
adhd.brief: Returns to the foundations to show how skewed real-world numbers fool simple averages and how variance and interquartile range capture the true spread.

adhd.label: Step 4 · Jumps to Ch. 7: Hypothesis Testing, P-Values & Statistical Power
adhd.brief: Unpacks the physical meaning of null hypotheses, Type I false alarms vs. Type II misses, and how to tell real treatment effect from luck.
